prompts.title: Body
prompts.text:
Create a new project: Loopforge Worker 01.

The three attached images show ONE character, not three alternatives. Use worker-01-front.02c6c68fda86b0c0.jpg as the authoritative design and A-pose. worker-01-back.c97d065cd1642436.jpg specifies the rear construction; worker-01-left.9e94fa650cdd2d38.jpg supports body depth. Keep the front pose/proportions if minor generated-view discrepancies occur. Do not combine these into a collage or generate extra characters.

Make a textured humanoid factory-worker robot faithful to this design: ordinary adult proportions, paired round cyan optics, a narrow grille mouth, fitted worn dark petrol-grey steel panels, restrained brass bearings, ribbed waist, coherent pelvis, tapered limbs, exposed mechanical hinges, five separate fingers including a thumb on each hand, and sturdy split-toe feet. Both hands are empty. No weapon, tool, carried object, backpack, base, floor or background geometry. No writing or supervisor insignia. Preserve mechanical form rather than smoothing it into a toy.

Maintain a symmetrical A-pose with arms separated from the body and a gap between the legs. Keep shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee and ankle joints clear enough to articulate. Preserve face, hand, foot and silhouette geometry; fine scratches, rivets and shallow grooves belong primarily in textures/normal maps.

Generate the body and textures, then create a separate remeshed candidate targeting about 25,000 triangles. Retain the detailed source separately. Do not sacrifice the hands or face just to hit the count. Use a compact PBR material set with base colour, normal, roughness and metalness where supported. Keep eye emission separate if supported; no baked cyan halo or dramatic studio shadows. Target 2K textures for the first review; retain better source maps separately if available.

Show the result from front, back and side before rigging. Report the actual triangle count and any unsupported requests. Stop after the model/remesh stage so I can inspect it.

prompts.title: Rig and motion
prompts.text:
Use the accepted Worker 01 delivery mesh and textures throughout. Rig a humanoid biped with Mixamo export naming; keep a neutral rigged A-pose. Report actual hierarchy and finger support. The accepted FBX bank has 24 skin joints, while an earlier GLB had 23: do not mix their raw animation tracks without retargeting. The vendor source has rigid fingers. Our offline derivative now adds ten rigid digit hinges (34 joints total) plus corrected motions. Preserve the vendor export as source and rerun offline fitting/cleanup after regeneration; do not claim the new Meshy export already includes those fixes. Broader rigid armor weighting remains scene-dependent.

Apply these catalog motions to the SAME body. Keep IDs in filenames and original embedded clip names. Export mesh, skin, materials and motion in GLB and FBX; export each clip independently if All Animations omits later additions.
- 0 Idle
- 2 Alert
- 25 Agree_Gesture
- 26 Angry_Stomp
- 31 Catching_Breath
- 36 Confused_Scratch (idle_scratch)
- 37 Discuss_While_Moving
- 47 Listening_Gesture
- 59 Victory_Cheer
- 106 Confident_Walk / owner UI name Hot Walk — CATHEXIS reference, not worker default
- 172 Electrocution_Reaction
- 181 Electrocuted_Fall
- 260 Push_Forward_and_Stop
- 576 Idle_Turn_Left
- 586 Idle_Turn_Right
- 611 Carry_Heavy_Walk
- 637 Injured_Walk_inplace
- 657 run_fast_10_inplace
- 692 walking_2_inplace

613 Casual_Walk_inplace was rejected for leg crossing. 692 is a replacement candidate, NOT certified collision-free: the original downloaded worker intersects its shins. Our corrected derivative is separate and has passed the recorded 120 Hz mesh checks. Keep source and corrected versions separate. Preserve intended Hot Walk crossover for CATHEXIS, but correct actual surface penetration on her own model.

Do not trust labels such as in-place without inspecting root travel. Catching Breath includes a running approach, Discuss While Moving travels, and fall clips finish displaced. Catalog names are source identity, not guaranteed gameplay meaning.

Still missing: afraid_recoil and exact work_cradle. Do not substitute a carry walk for machine work. If custom motion is unavailable in the current Agent UI, report that and preserve the successful exports for offline authoring.

Report each filename, hash if available, triangle/joint counts, embedded clips/durations and root translation/rotation. A working browser preview is not proof of a complete downloaded asset.

Offline acting requirements (after source export): Confused Scratch must reach the scalp with curled fingertips. Injured Walk braces the right thigh with the right palm. Agree Gesture presents opposed palms for clapping. Angry Stomp folds the arms at different heights/depths and uncrosses them without cutting through one another. Resting hands face inward with relaxed fingers and forearm/wrist rotation. Electrocuted Fall must keep both complete hands above the fixed scene floor. These are locally authored corrections, not Meshy catalog guarantees; preserve the source for comparison.

Scratch correction must preserve the original elbow hinge and the puzzled gesture between the two scratch beats; fit contact using shoulder clearance and palm-axis wrist flexion. Fall left-arm correction must preserve source elbow and wrist alignment, lifting the whole arm to clear the floor instead of forcing the palm down. Review joint silhouette from multiple angles as well as triangle intersections. These constraints are checked locally after Meshy export.

prompts.title: Afraid
prompts.text:
CUSTOM / OFFLINE CONTACT BRIEF — not supplied in the current bank.

An industrial robot notices a threat in front, recoils without stepping, lowers its torso, raises both forearms to shield its face and holds a fearful guarded pose briefly. Its head makes a small wary look, then it cautiously lowers its hands to the opening neutral stance. Feet planted, no root travel. Fear and submission, not combat. No prop.

prompts.title: Work cradle
prompts.text:
CUSTOM / OFFLINE CONTACT BRIEF — not supplied in the current bank.

A factory robot works standing at a fixed waist-high fixture. Feet stay planted. It leans forward, braces a small cradle with its left hand, reaches with its right hand to a latch, presses and turns it with brief effort, then releases both hands and returns to neutral. Clear anticipation, contact, effort and release. No lifting or root travel. Animate body only.
